subject: TTFT & streaming cadence - follow up / SLO discussion
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Bennett <tbennett@acme-retail.com>, Sofia Ramirez <s.ramirez@acme-retail.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-20T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT & streaming cadence - follow up / SLO discussion

Hi Tom / Sofia —

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on product UX and perf expectations. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we're all synced: 

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Primary goal: interactive chat experiences (customer support agents + end-user chat) with streaming responses.
- TTFT target: 200–250ms for first token on typical user prompts (avg ~100–200 tokens).
- Streaming: SSE preferred for web clients; WebSocket acceptable for native apps. Key requirement is consistent chunk cadence (target ~200–300ms between chunks for a smooth typing experience).
- Throughput / concurrency: typical steady-state ~25 qps, expected peak bursts up to ~200 qps; concurrent sessions up to ~300 active users at peak (we'll clarify exact concurrency model below).
- SLA ask: can Redwood guarantee TTFT at target under the peak pattern? Also want guidance on instance sizing, batching behavior, and fallback model variants.

Requested from Acme for qualification
- Representative sample payloads (typical prompt lengths, system messages).
- Expected concurrency model (sessions vs requests per second) and acceptable latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99).
- Any constraints on connection type (SSE vs WS) or ability to accept chunk cadence constraints.

Attachments: Redwood-SLO-checklist.pdf (attached) — a short checklist of questions we use when qualifying TTFT/streaming SLOs.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with Aditya (infra/serving) to validate TTFT numbers and streaming cadence. Can you share 2 slots that work this week?
2) Acme to send sample payloads + a short note on concurrency model (sessions vs QPS) so we can run a targeted load profile.
3) Redwood to deliver a short MMP (mutual action plan) and draft SLA language after the deep-dive.

Happy to adjust — let me know availability.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

--
Redwood-SLO-checklist.pdf (attached): one-page checklist covering TTFT targets, chunk cadence, throughput, and connection preferences.

From: Tom Bennett <tbennett@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ramirez <s.ramirez@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming cadence - follow up / SLO discussion

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirm TTFT target: we should design for <= 250ms p50 and aim for p95 under 400ms for the first token on our standard prompt (avg ~120 tokens). p99 can be relaxed if we have clear fallbacks.
- Streaming cadence: SSE is our preference for the web widget; chunk cadence of ~200–300ms feels right. We care more about smoothness than tiny chunks — 2–3 chunks/sec is our rough target for medium responses (200–400 chars).
- Traffic profile: baseline 20–30 qps, predictable daytime peaks up to ~200 qps for limited bursts (holiday promos). Concurrent active sessions during peaks: ~150–300 (depends on feature flag rollout).

Question: can Redwood provide an initial runbook or sizing guidance (GPU tiers / concurrency per instance) that shows measurable TTFT at 200 qps? If possible, include differences between SSE vs WS (any hop/latency delta) and preferred client best practices (keep-alive, max idle timeout).

I'll pull together sample payloads and a short doc on our concurrency model this afternoon and upload to the Drive link you shared.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Bennett
Head of Product, Conversational Experience | Acme Retail
Tom.Bennett@acme-retail.com | +1 312-555-0102
